title.narrative: Emergency cholera response in Renk (Gesundes Afrika)

description.narrative:
This project aims to reduce the incidence and spread of cholera in Renk County, South Sudan, by targeting 30,000 vulnerable individuals, including refugees, returnees, and host communities in high-risk areas. To reduce the incidence and spread of cholera, we will employ a multi-sectoral approach focusing on rapid response and Containment of the outbreak by enhancing surveilance using the trained health workers, provision of infection prevention and control (IPC) supplies and maintaining the IPC measures, setting up of Oral rehydration therapy (ORT) points, carry out contact tracing and conduct Oral Cholera Vaccination (ORV) campaigns when vaccines are readily available. The Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) intervention will focus on provision of household water treatment purifiers, construction of semi-permanent units of latrines at transit centers and emergency temporary latrines at high-risk communities and we will scale risk communication and community engagement (RC&CE) to raise awareness on cholera outbreak and improve hygiene practices by providing supplies such as multi-Purpose laundry soap, Buckets for water collection and storage and handwashing stations.
The project will be implemented jointly by Cordaid and Africa Development Aid (ADA) over a six-month period, starting in November 2024, subject to timely resource availability. A robust M&E system will be in place to ensure quality assurance and accountability. We will monitor key indicators, conduct regular field visits, and analyze data to inform decision-making and adapt our strategies as needed.
To ensure long-term sustainability, we will focus on capacity building of local communities, including health workers and hygiene promoters. We will also promote community ownership of interventions, such as through community-led maintenance of sanitation facilities. Additionally, we will strengthen partnerships with local authorities and other organizations to ensure continued support and resource allocation for health services in Renk.

Through the intervention, 8,400 children of ages between 0 – 5 years will be targeted because of their immature immune system making them vulnerable to infections.
Beneficiaries Total beneficiaries: 30,000 Women: 10,500 Children: 8,400 Men: 9,000 Elderly: 600 Disabled: 1,500

To reduce the incidence and stop spread of cholera in Renk County, Upper Nile State, South Sudan, by strengthening water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services, improving access to healthcare, and promoting community awareness and participation.
